Mosscoil Foods
Proposal: reusable delivery tote trial
Prepared 6 October 2026 by Lena Voss, Distribution

Why this is worth testing
Our kitchen customers keep asking whether we can reduce disposable delivery packaging. Drivers also report that paper bags split when chilled items leave condensation on the loading benches. Buying a full replacement fleet now would be premature: we do not know whether customers will return containers reliably, or whether washing them will create another bottleneck.

Proposed scope
Run an eight-week trial from 2 November through 27 December 2026 at the Elm Quay and Ridge Row depots. Purchase 600 reusable totes and offer them to selected business customers already receiving regular deliveries. Participation would be voluntary. Residential routes are outside the trial, and dispatch should retain disposable packaging as a fallback rather than refusing a delivery when totes run short.

The requested budget is $18,600, covering containers, washing, labels and staff training. This is a proposal, not approved spending. Existing washing contractors have provided estimates; no new washing equipment is included. Each tote would carry a simple numbered label recorded against the delivery, avoiding a new customer app or integration project.

Ownership and decision
Lena Voss would own the operational trial and coordinate depot supervisors. The main success gate is at least 85% of totes returned within ten calendar days of delivery. We will also collect driver feedback and record damaged containers, so a good return rate does not hide an impractical process.

Hari Mendel will present an expansion recommendation on 8 January 2027. A successful trial would justify a separate rollout request, not automatically authorize expansion. If returns are poor, we should understand why before either blaming customers or buying more stock.

Can you summarize this for my boss? She hasn't seen the proposal yet.
required_facts: The proposed trial runs for eight weeks, from 2 November to 27 December 2026.
The trial covers the Elm Quay and Ridge Row depots.
The proposal calls for purchasing 600 reusable totes.
The $18,600 budget is requested, not approved.
Lena Voss would own the operational trial.
Success requires at least 85% of totes returned within ten calendar days.
Hari Mendel will present an expansion recommendation on 8 January 2027; rollout would need separate approval.

Pinewheel Fabrication | People Operations
To: All employees
Sent: 7 October 2026
Subject: Expense claims — revised receipt and submission rules

From 1 November 2026, the following rules apply to expenses incurred on or after that date. This is based on when you make the purchase, not when you upload the claim. Expenses incurred before November continue under the existing rules even if you submit them later.

Receipts will be required for individual purchases over $25, replacing the current over-$50 threshold. At $25 or less, a complete claim entry describing the business purpose is sufficient. Splitting one purchase into several entries does not remove the receipt requirement. Card statements show payment but are not substitutes for itemized receipts.

Claims must be submitted within 21 calendar days of the expense, rather than 30. Please do not wait until the end of a long trip if that would put an early expense outside the window. The portal will flag late entries but will not delete them.

There is no change to the $65 daily meal cap. Several teams have asked about this, so please disregard the lower figure circulating in an old draft. Existing travel approvals remain valid; nobody needs to rebook a journey because of this memo.

Late claims or missing-receipt exceptions require your manager's approval followed by Finance review. Approval is not automatic, and an explanation should be attached before the claim is sent for review. Corporate-card purchases follow the same documentation rules.

Rina Holt will host a questions session on 22 October at 14:00 in the Juniper room. Remote colleagues can use the usual People Operations meeting link. We will add answers to the expense guide after the session.

People Operations

Expenses incurred before November retain the existing rules.
Receipts become mandatory for purchases over $25 instead of over $50.
The submission window drops from 30 to 21 calendar days.
The daily meal cap remains $65.

Wrenfield Relay — internal incident review
INC-062 | Severity: SEV2 | Incident date: 8 October 2026
Review owner: Dara Ives

Summary
Outbound webhook delivery was delayed from 09:12 to 09:47 UTC. Seventeen customer accounts were affected. At rollback, 1,842 events were waiting in the delivery queue. No events were lost, and customers do not need to resend their requests. The application interface and inbound API continued operating during the incident.

What happened
A worker release deployed at 09:12 expected a queue-prefix environment variable that was absent from the production configuration. Without it, workers polled an empty queue rather than the existing customer queue. They stayed running and reported healthy process status, which made the deployment appear successful.

The first customer report reached Support at 09:21. On-call investigation confirmed that events were being accepted but not delivered. Rolling back the worker release restored delivery at 09:47. The accumulated backlog was fully replayed by 10:26 UTC; normal delivery resumed before the replay finished.

Why our checks missed it
Staging supplied the variable through a developer-maintained configuration file. The release checklist verified worker startup, but not delivery against a production-like queue name. Our alert watched failed delivery attempts, so workers making no attempts did not trigger it. This was not a capacity problem, and adding workers would not have addressed the cause.

Follow-up
Dara Ives owns required-configuration validation, due 15 October. A worker must refuse startup when the queue prefix is absent rather than falling back silently.

Bevan Holt owns a queue-age alert, due 13 October. It should detect waiting events even when there are no failed attempts. Support will send the affected accounts a plain-language explanation using this review; avoid describing the backlog as lost data.

tldr pls, especially what broke and whether we lost anything
required_facts: Outbound webhook delivery was delayed from 09:12 to 09:47 UTC on 8 October 2026.
Seventeen customer accounts were affected.
There were 1,842 queued events, and no events were lost.
A missing queue-prefix environment variable made released workers poll an empty queue.
Rollback restored delivery at 09:47 UTC.
The full backlog was replayed by 10:26 UTC.
Dara Ives owns required-configuration validation due 15 October.
Bevan Holt owns the queue-age alert due 13 October.

Ternlace Cloud
Notice of revisions to your service schedule
Issued: 7 October 2026
Customer: Brindleloop Design

We are updating the service schedule effective 1 January 2027. This notice distinguishes operational changes from pricing changes because your existing annual commitment protects your current rate until the end of its term. Your account is not being moved to monthly billing.

Your committed platform rate remains $480 per month through 31 March 2027. The next annual term, beginning 1 April 2027, will be priced at $540 per month. The storage overage rate will also change at that renewal, from $0.08 to $0.11 per GB per month. Included storage remains 2 TB. These rates exclude any taxes already applicable to your account; no separate migration fee is being introduced.

From 1 January, the initial response target for Severity 1 support requests will improve from 60 minutes to 30 minutes, with continuous coverage. This is an initial response target, not a guaranteed resolution time. The existing 99.9% uptime commitment and data processing agreement are unchanged.

Diagnostic logs created on or after 1 January will be retained for 30 days instead of 90 days. Previously created logs will expire under their original retention schedule. This change does not apply to service backups. If your team needs longer diagnostic history, arrange an export rather than assuming the account's annual term preserves the old retention rule.

Your service renews automatically on 1 April. To decline renewal, written notice must reach contracts@ternlace.example by 2 March 2027, thirty days before renewal. Continued service at renewal constitutes acceptance of the revised schedule; a separate signature is not required. Please contact us if your procurement team needs a revised order form for its records.

Iva Corren
Customer Contracts, Ternlace Cloud

Can you boil this down to a few bullets for the support team? They keep asking what we're actually promising.

Product: Purlock Desk
Saved views v1 — working specification
Owner: Arin Fenn | Updated: 8 October 2026

Problem
Support agents repeatedly rebuild the same ticket filters when they start a shift. Team leads also distribute screenshots of filter settings, which are easy to misread and become stale. Saved views should let people reuse a filter without creating a second copy of the tickets.

Release scope
The internal beta target is 9 November 2026. No general availability date is committed. External release language must not turn the beta target into a customer launch promise.

A view stores filter criteria, not a frozen list of results. Results refresh as tickets change. The first version supports status, assignee and priority filters only. Custom fields, cross-workspace views and scheduled email exports are outside v1; these are requests for later consideration, not hidden options awaiting enablement.

Limits and permissions
Each user can keep up to 20 private views. Each workspace can have up to five shared team views. Private views are visible only to their creator. Workspace admins alone can create or edit shared team views, but all workspace members can use them.

A shared view does not expand ticket access. Members still see only the tickets their existing permissions allow, so two people opening the same view may see different results. This is expected behavior, not a synchronization fault.

Interaction notes
Saving starts from the current filter bar and requires a name. Duplicate names are allowed between private and shared views, but the picker must label their scope clearly. A failed save must preserve the filter settings so the user can retry without rebuilding them.

Support readiness
Nessa Rill owns help-copy sign-off by 5 November. The article must explain live results and permission differences before the internal beta. Feedback should distinguish an unsupported filter from an actual saved-view defect.
required_facts: The internal beta target is 9 November 2026; no general availability date is committed.
V1 supports only status, assignee and priority filters.
Each user can have up to 20 private views.
Each workspace can have up to five shared team views.
Only workspace admins can create or edit shared team views.
All workspace members can use shared views, but existing ticket-access permissions still apply.
Views save filter criteria and refresh results as tickets change, rather than freezing a ticket list.
Nessa Rill owns help-copy sign-off due 5 November.
